title: Isaiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 28.

questions.question: In Isaiah 28, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Woe to the crown of pride
In that day shall the LORD of hosts
But they also have erred through wine
For precept must be upon precept
questions.correctAnswer: Woe to the crown of pride
questions.explanation: This appears first in the chapter as stated in Isaiah 28:1.

questions.question: What does the Lord have according to Isaiah 28:2?
questions.correctAnswer: A mighty and strong one
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:2 states, 'the Lord hath a mighty and strong one'.

questions.question: What shall happen to the crown of pride according to Isaiah 28:3?
options: It shall be trodden under feet
It shall be adorned with jewels
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be trodden under feet
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:3 explicitly states that 'the crown of pride...shall be trodden under feet'.

questions.question: What is described as a fading flower in Isaiah 28:4?
questions.correctAnswer: The glorious beauty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:4 refers to 'the glorious beauty' as a fading flower.

questions.question: In that day, what shall the LORD of hosts be for His people according to Isaiah 28:5?
questions.correctAnswer: A crown of glory
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:5 states that 'the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory'.

questions.question: What is said about the priests and prophets in Isaiah 28:7?
options: They are out of the way through strong drink
They lead the people in righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: They are out of the way through strong drink
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:7 mentions that the priests and prophets 'have erred through wine...they are out of the way through strong drink'.

questions.question: What is mentioned as full of vomit in Isaiah 28:8?
questions.correctAnswer: All tables
questions.explanation: According to Isaiah 28:8, 'all tables are full of vomit and filthiness'.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 28:9, whom shall the Lord teach knowledge?
options: Them that are weaned from the milk
questions.correctAnswer: Them that are weaned from the milk
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:9 asks, 'Whom shall he teach knowledge? ...them that are weaned from the milk'.

questions.question: What must be upon precept according to Isaiah 28:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Precept must be upon precept
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:10 states, 'For precept must be upon precept'.

questions.question: In Isaiah 28:6, what is given to him that sitteth in judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: A spirit of judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:6 states, 'And for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment'.

questions.question: In Isaiah 28:5, who will the LORD of hosts be for?
questions.correctAnswer: The residue of his people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:5 mentions that the LORD of hosts will be for 'the residue of his people'.

questions.question: Is it true that the crown of pride is associated with the drunkards of Ephraim?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:1 states, 'Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim'.

questions.question: Is it true that all tables are clean according to Isaiah 28:8?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:8 states that 'there is no place clean', indicating that all tables are not clean.

questions.question: Is it false that the Lord is described as a mighty and weak one in Isaiah 28:2?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:2 describes the Lord as a 'mighty and strong one', not weak.

questions.question: Is it false that the priests are described as being filled with strong drink in Isaiah 28:7?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:7 states that the priests 'are swallowed up of wine', indicating they are not filled with it in a positive manner.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 28:11, how will God speak to the people?
options: With stammering lips and another tongue
With a loud voice and thunder
With a gentle whisper and calm words
questions.correctAnswer: With stammering lips and another tongue
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:11 states that God will speak to the people with stammering lips and another tongue, indicating a foreign or unfamiliar language.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 28:13 promise will happen if the people reject the 'precept upon precept' teaching commanded in verse 12?
options: They might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken
They will find peace and rest
They will prosper and be blessed
They shall be lifted up and honored
questions.correctAnswer: They might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:13 explains that because the people would not listen to the rest and refreshing offered in verse 12, the word of the LORD was given 'precept upon precept' so that they might go and fall backward, be broken, and snared.

questions.question: In Isaiah 28:16, what is described as a sure foundation laid in Zion?
options: A tried stone, a precious corner stone
questions.correctAnswer: A tried stone, a precious corner stone
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:16 states that the Lord lays in Zion a foundation of a tried stone, a precious corner stone, and a sure foundation.

questions.question: How do Isaiah 28:15 and Isaiah 28:18 relate regarding the covenant with death?
options: Verse 15 describes making a covenant with death; verse 18 says this covenant shall be disannulled
Verse 15 promises protection through the covenant; verse 18 encourages keeping it
Verse 15 warns against the covenant; verse 18 praises the covenant
Both verses affirm the strength of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 15 describes making a covenant with death; verse 18 says this covenant shall be disannulled
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:15 records the people making a covenant with death and lies as refuge, but verse 18 declares that this covenant with death shall be disannulled and the agreement with hell will not stand.

questions.question: What is the practical implication of Isaiah 28:12's 'rest' and 'refreshing' for the weary?
options: Trusting God's promise provides spiritual rest even when circumstances are hard
Only physical rest can ease weariness
Ignoring God's word leads to rest
Rest is achieved by making covenants with lies
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God's promise provides spiritual rest even when circumstances are hard
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:12 offers rest and refreshing through God's word, implying that spiritual trust brings true rest for the weary despite life's difficulties.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 28:17, what will the 'hail' do?
options: Sweep away the refuge of lies
questions.correctAnswer: Sweep away the refuge of lies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:17 describes that hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, showing God's judgment against falsehood.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 28:14 characterize the leaders in Jerusalem?
options: Scornful men who rule the people
questions.correctAnswer: Scornful men who rule the people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:14 addresses the leaders as scornful men ruling the people, indicating their pride and rejection of God's word.

questions.question: What imagery in Isaiah 28:20 illustrates insufficiency and discomfort?
options: The bed is shorter than a man can stretch himself on it, and the covering narrower than he can wrap himself in it
A river that dries up in summer
questions.correctAnswer: The bed is shorter than a man can stretch himself on it, and the covering narrower than he can wrap himself in it
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:20 uses the imagery of an inadequate bed and covering to illustrate the insufficiency of their plans or refuge.

questions.question: What is the consequence described in Isaiah 28:19 for those relying on their covenant with death?
options: The overflowing scourge will take them morning by morning, day and night
They will be shielded from all harm
They will gain honor among nations
questions.correctAnswer: The overflowing scourge will take them morning by morning, day and night
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:19 warns that the scourge will continually pass over and take those who rely on their covenant with death.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 28:13 describe the teaching method of the word of the LORD?
options: Precept upon precept; line upon line; here a little, and there a little
questions.correctAnswer: Precept upon precept; line upon line; here a little, and there a little
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:13 describes the word of the LORD as given step by step, teaching carefully and incrementally.

questions.question: What attitude does Isaiah 28:15 reveal about the people's trust?
options: They trusted in lies and falsehood as refuge
They fully trusted in God’s promises
questions.correctAnswer: They trusted in lies and falsehood as refuge
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:15 states the people made lies their refuge and hid themselves under falsehood rather than trusting God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'precious corner stone' mentioned in Isaiah 28:16 for believers?
options: He that believeth shall not make haste
It will be rejected by all
It is a symbol of destruction
questions.correctAnswer: He that believeth shall not make haste
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:16 promises that those who believe in the precious corner stone will not be in haste, signifying confidence and stability.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 28:11-12, what was the people's response to the rest and refreshing offered by God?
questions.correctAnswer: They would not hear
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:12 clearly states that despite God's offer of rest and refreshing, the people would not hear.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 28:13 indicates that the word of the LORD was given in a way to cause the people to understand and be strengthened.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:13 explains the word of the LORD was given 'precept upon precept' so that the people might learn step by step, though their rejection led to their downfall, the method was intended to teach and strengthen.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 28:19 suggests that the scourge will be a one-time event affecting the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:19 says the scourge will pass over morning by morning, day and night, indicating continual and repeated judgment, not a one-time event.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 28.

questions.question: What does the LORD do in Isaiah 28:21?
options: He rises up as in mount Perazim
He brings peace to the earth
He speaks to the drunkards of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: He rises up as in mount Perazim
questions.explanation: This is stated in Isaiah 28:21, which mentions the LORD rising up as in mount Perazim.

questions.question: What is the consequence of mocking according to Isaiah 28:22?
options: Your bands will be made strong
questions.correctAnswer: Your bands will be made strong
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:22 warns not to mock, implying that doing so will lead to stronger bands.

questions.question: What does the plowman do according to Isaiah 28:24?
options: He plows all day to sow
questions.correctAnswer: He plows all day to sow
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:24 poses a rhetorical question affirming that the plowman indeed plows all day to sow.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 28:29 say about the work of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: It is wonderful in counsel
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:29 states that the work of the LORD of hosts is wonderful in counsel and excellent in working.

questions.question: What should the people do according to Isaiah 28:23?
options: Ignore the words of the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Listen and hear my voice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:23 urges the people to give ear and hear the voice of the speaker.

questions.question: How are the fitches threshed according to Isaiah 28:27?
questions.correctAnswer: With a staff
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:27 explains that fitches are beaten out with a staff, contrasting their treatment with that of wheat.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'תְּבוּאָה' (tevu'ah) in Isaiah 28:25 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Harvest
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 28:25, 'תְּבוּאָה' refers to the harvest, indicating the outcome of sowing.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 28:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:10 shows parallelism with the repetition of 'precept upon precept, line upon line'.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment seen in Isaiah 28:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 25:31-32
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:31-32 connects to the theme of judgment, echoing the call for accountability seen in Isaiah 28:21.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the promise of a cornerstone mentioned in Isaiah 28:16?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Peter 2:6
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 2:6 references Christ as the cornerstone, fulfilling the promise in Isaiah 28:16.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Isaiah 28:21?
questions.correctAnswer: An explanation of judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:20, preceding verse 21, contains a description of the judgment and conditions leading to it.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 28:9 ask regarding the people?
options: What is the way to wisdom?
What is the covenant with death?
questions.correctAnswer: Who will teach knowledge?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:9 questions whom the LORD will teach knowledge, focusing on the readiness of the people.

questions.question: What is stated about the priests and prophets in Isaiah 28:7?
options: They have erred through strong drink
They are beloved by the people
questions.correctAnswer: They have erred through strong drink
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:7 declares that the priests and prophets have erred due to strong drink, leading them astray.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's work is described as strange in Isaiah 28:21.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:21 describes the LORD's work as a strange work, highlighting its unusual nature.

questions.question: True or False: The drunkards of Ephraim are praised in Isaiah 28:1.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:1 pronounces a woe to the drunkards of Ephraim, indicating condemnation rather than praise.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 28:16 teach about God’s provision for salvation?
options: God provides a sure foundation for faith through the precious cornerstone
Salvation is earned by human works and covenant agreements
God’s foundation is uncertain and requires human effort to stabilize
The cornerstone refers primarily to Israel’s political leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God provides a sure foundation for faith through the precious cornerstone
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:16 states that God lays a 'tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation' in Zion, indicating that salvation rests securely on God’s provision, not human works.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is taught in Isaiah 28:7 regarding the leaders of Israel?
options: Leaders stumble in judgment due to intoxication and error
Leaders are infallible and guided perfectly by God
Sin is only found among the common people, not leaders
Leaders intentionally lead people to righteousness apart from God
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders stumble in judgment due to intoxication and error
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:7 explains that priests and prophets err through strong drink, stumbling in judgment, illustrating the sinful failure of religious leadership.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s judgment and righteousness is taught in Isaiah 28:17?
options: God applies judgment and righteousness with precision and removes false refuges
Judgment is arbitrary and favors those with political power
Righteousness is secondary to human agreements with death
God ignores lies and falsehood in His judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God applies judgment and righteousness with precision and removes false refuges
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:17 shows God laying judgment to the line and righteousness to the plummet, sweeping away lies and false refuges, indicating precise and holy judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 28:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:21 describes the LORD rising up to do His 'strange work' and 'strange act,' demonstrating His sovereign control over history and judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Isaiah 28:29?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:29 describes the LORD of hosts as 'wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working,' highlighting His divine wisdom in all His actions.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 28:11-12 connect to the New Testament theme of Pentecost and the gift of tongues?
options: God’s speaking with stammering lips and another tongue prefigures the Spirit’s gift of tongues to communicate His word
The passage condemns all foreign languages as confusing and evil
It predicts the destruction of all linguistic diversity
It emphasizes that only Hebrew is the true language of God
questions.correctAnswer: God’s speaking with stammering lips and another tongue prefigures the Spirit’s gift of tongues to communicate His word
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:11-12 speaks of God communicating in another tongue, which foreshadows the New Testament Pentecost event where the Spirit enabled speaking in diverse languages (Acts 2:4).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Isaiah 28:15-18 have with the doctrine of atonement?
options: It contrasts human false covenants with God's true covenant foundation in Christ
It teaches that death and hell have ultimate authority over believers
It demands that covenant with death is the way to salvation
It denies any hope of resurrection or deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts human false covenants with God's true covenant foundation in Christ
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:15-18 condemns making covenants with death and falsehood, but proclaims God’s foundation stone in Zion, which Christian theology understands as Christ, God's true covenant for salvation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Isaiah 28:9 and Isaiah 28:10 teach about human spiritual maturity?
options: Spiritual understanding comes progressively through careful teaching, not sudden revelation
Spiritual maturity is irrelevant for salvation
Only miraculous gifts can teach spiritual knowledge
Doctrine is too complex for anyone to understand
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual understanding comes progressively through careful teaching, not sudden revelation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:9-10 highlights that God teaches the weaned with 'precept upon precept, line upon line,' indicating a progressive, patient instruction toward spiritual maturity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 28:1 and Isaiah 28:7 teach about the nature of human sin?
options: Sin leads to pride, intoxication, and failure even among leaders
Sin is primarily external and does not affect leaders
Pride is always beneficial for societal leadership
Intoxication is not related to spiritual blindness
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to pride, intoxication, and failure even among leaders
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:1 condemns the 'crown of pride' and drunkenness in Ephraim, and 28:7 shows priests and prophets erring through strong drink, illustrating pervasive sin affecting all classes.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 28:23-26 teach about God's providential order in creation and instruction?
options: God’s instruction is orderly and purposeful, like the farmer’s careful sowing
God’s work is chaotic and lacks discretion
Human efforts alone determine the success of sowing and teaching
God’s providence is irrelevant to daily work
questions.correctAnswer: God’s instruction is orderly and purposeful, like the farmer’s careful sowing
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:23-26 uses the metaphor of the farmer’s methodical sowing to illustrate God’s wise and purposeful teaching and providential care.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Isaiah 28:11-13 shows God’s word is confusing and ineffective. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s word is purposeful, using difficult speech to judge and sift the people
God’s word is arbitrary and without meaning
God’s communication is only for the elite and excludes others
The passage encourages ignoring God’s word
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word is purposeful, using difficult speech to judge and sift the people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:11-13 explains that God’s confusing speech serves as judgment because the people rejected His clear teaching, showing intentional divine discipline, not ineffectiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s judgment is taught in Isaiah 28:22?
options: God has decreed a consuming judgment upon the whole earth
God’s judgment is limited to Israel alone
God is unwilling to punish sin
Judgment can be avoided by mocking God
questions.correctAnswer: God has decreed a consuming judgment upon the whole earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:22 declares that God has determined a consumption, a decisive judgment, upon the whole earth, showing the universal scope of His justice.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s justice and righteousness is taught in Isaiah 28:18?
options: God will annul false covenants and bring judgment upon those trusting in death
God accepts covenants made with death and hell
Righteousness is optional in God’s covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God will annul false covenants and bring judgment upon those trusting in death
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:18 states that the covenant with death and agreement with hell will not stand, but be disannulled, emphasizing God’s justice against false trust.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 28:4 and Isaiah 28:1 teach about the consequences of pride and worldly indulgence?
options: Pride and drunkenness lead to temporal beauty that fades quickly and judgment
Pride leads to eternal glory without consequence
Fading beauty is unrelated to moral failure
questions.correctAnswer: Pride and drunkenness lead to temporal beauty that fades quickly and judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:1 and 28:4 describe the crown of pride and drunkenness as a fading flower, indicating the fleeting nature of sinful glory and impending judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s enabling grace is taught in Isaiah 28:6?
options: God gives a spirit of judgment and strength to those who govern and fight
Human strength alone secures victory and judgment
God’s grace is passive and non-involvement in human affairs
Strength and judgment are unrelated to divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: God gives a spirit of judgment and strength to those who govern and fight
questions.explanation: Isaiah 28:6 states the LORD will be a spirit of judgment and strength to rulers and warriors, highlighting God’s active empowering grace in leadership and battle.
